content: In Lamentations, what is new every morning?
explanation: Great is His faithfulness. “They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness!” (Lamentations 3:23, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, what does the writer call great in the LORD?
explanation: His mercies never fail. “great is Your faithfulness!” (Lamentations 3:23, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, to whom is the LORD good?
explanation: And to the soul who seeks Him. “The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul who seeks Him.” (Lamentations 3:25, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, why are we not consumed?
explanation: His mercies never fail. “Because of the loving devotion of the LORD we are not consumed, for His mercies never fail.” (Lamentations 3:22, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, the ruined city once full of people has become like what?
explanation: Jerusalem had fallen. “She who was great among the nations has become a widow.” (Lamentations 1:1, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, how is it good to wait for the LORD's salvation?
explanation: Trust God in hard times. “It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.” (Lamentations 3:26, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, after examining our ways, what should we do?
explanation: Repentance brings hope. “Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.” (Lamentations 3:40, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, what does the people's prayer ask God to renew?
explanation: Restore us to Yourself. “renew our days as of old” (Lamentations 5:21, BSB)

content: In Lamentations, the princess of the provinces has become what?
explanation: The city's glory was gone. “The princess of the provinces has become a slave.” (Lamentations 1:1, BSB)
